exposure: implementation of a more active management strategy for late-term pregnancies (offering induction from 41+0 weeks or an individual plan aiming at birth or active labour no later than 42+0 weeks)
outcome: composite adverse peri/neonatal outcome (including/excluding NICU admission)
admission to a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) >=4 days
cohort: The study included 150,370 women with singleton pregnancies lasting 41+0 weeks or more with a fetus in cephalic presentation, excluding elective cesarean sections.
finding: A more active management of late-term pregnancies was associated with a decrease in peri/neonatal deaths and composite adverse peri/neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: The rate of emergency cesarean sections increased from 10.5% to 11.9% with the implementation of the more active management strategy.
gest_age: Pregnancies lasting 41+0 weeks or more, with mean gestational age at birth decreasing from 290.7 days to 289.6 days in the study periods.
